issues.text: The commonest reason they were given was that the patient had not consented. / most often told the patient had not consented / commonest reason given was no patient consent
issues.problem: Lack of consent was tied with staff unavailability (both 46.2%); 'commonest' / 'most often' implies it was the single leading reason.
issues.source_says: The main reasons given ... include: lack of patient consent (46.2%) and unavailability of a team member (46.2%).
issues.replacement: x: 'One of the two commonest reasons they were given was that the patient had not consented.' linkedin: 'One of the two commonest reasons they were given (alongside no team member being available) was lack of the patient's consent.' bluesky/threads: 'often told the patient had not consented'. visual_text and alt_text: 'one of the two commonest reasons given was no patient consent'.

issues.text: Column 2 and 3 in teal with label 'No clear difference' (third column: 'Non-carers (comparison)')
issues.problem: Non-carers are the reference group; labelling them 'No clear difference' is meaningless and could be read as a finding.
issues.source_says: RRs are relative to noncaregiving controls.
issues.replacement: Label column 3 'Comparison group' only; keep 'No clear difference' on column 2.

issues.text: Only 4 trials have tested respite breaks for carers of people with dementia
issues.problem: Present tense implies current count; the review dates from 2014 with no update found.
issues.source_says: Four trials are now included in the review (2014).
issues.replacement: A 2014 Cochrane review found only 4 trials of respite breaks for carers of people with dementia, and the evidence was very low quality.

issues.text: Our view: judge carer support first by the carer's health.
issues.problem: Posts are in Alasdair's first person; 'Our' implies an organisational position.
issues.replacement: My view: judge carer support first by the carer's health.
